item.title: City slump again as Arsenal extend Premier League lead
item.description: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring against Hull at the Emirates Stadium (Henry Nicholls) Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points. Enzo Maresca's men desperately needed a victory at the City Ground to keep pace with the in-form champions, who have taken 27 points from a possible 30, but lost 3-1. City had a mountain to climb after finding themselves 2-0 down in the 18th minute following goals from defender Jair Cunha and forward Liam Delap. The visitors were much improved after the break and Rayan Cherki cut the deficit with an emphatic strike into the roof of the net. But Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute, rifling home with his left foot past the outstretched hand of Gianluigi Donnarumma to earn his side breathing room. Forest manager Oliver Glasner sprinted down the touchline to celebrate with his team, who had not managed to score a single Premier League goal at home before Saturday. City, who won their first seven league games under new manager Maresca, know that even if they close the gap to Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain. The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules -- with a huge points deduction one potential punishment. - Odegaard strikes - Earlier, Arsenal made hard work of beating struggling Hull to underline their title credentials on the eve of the international break. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute. Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal's rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher's finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range. Arsenal manager Arteta praised his players but wants them to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games. "We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient," he said. "That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes." item.title: Delap double condemns Man City to third straight defeat
item.description: Liam Delap scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City (Darren Staples) Manchester City slumped to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday as Liam Delap's double lifted Nottingham Forest out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win at the City Ground. Oliver Glasner's men had not scored at home at all this season, but pounced on City's defensive errors to strike twice in the first 20 minutes through Jair Cunha and Delap. Rayan Cherki's stunning strike gave City hope, but their title challenge is rapidly wilting even before the potential effects of a major points deduction. Delap sealed just Forest's second win of the season with an incredible strike in off the post on the night that could launch his career for the two-time European champions, after a difficult start since his club-record £50 million ($67 million) move from Chelsea. Defeat leaves City six points adrift of leaders Arsenal and with questions over whether the uncertainty surrounding the club is playing a part in their on-field slump. Found guilty on over 100 Premier League charges of breaking financial rules, the 10-time English champions face a severe points penalty unless they can overturn that verdict on appeal. Glasner warned his players he would make big changes after a disappointing start to his reign saw them start the match in the bottom three. The Austrian got the response he craved as Forest burst out of the blocks to pounce on City's sloppiness at the back. - Clinical Forest - Cunha robbed Josko Gvardiol midway inside the City half and was allowed to bear down on goal before slotting past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Forest's first home goal in 511 minutes was celebrated wildly at the City Ground with owner Evangelos Marinakis jumping out of his chair in celebration. Elliott Anderson had a night to forget on his first return to Forest since a reported £116 million move to City. Xaver Schlager beat Anderson to the ball in midfield and set Delap running from inside his own half before unleashing an unstoppable drive past Donnarumma for his first home goal for the club. Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games in charge of a new club in a blistering start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. However, he has been hit with the task of trying to keep his players motivated when they do not know if they will even be in the English top-flight next season. Maresca showed his frustration with a double change at half-time with the introduction of Nico O'Reilly and Matheus Nunes helping to spark a brief City rally. Cherki smashed home a sweet strike from Jeremy Doku's deflected cross to halve the arrears. Erling Haaland then nearly levelled when the Norwegian flashed a shot just wide. item.title: Real Madrid scout 18-year-old English midfield talent wanted by Manchester United – report
item.description: Real Madrid scout 18-year-old English midfield talent wanted by Manchester United – report According to TeamTalk , Real Madrid have scouted Leicester City teenage midfielder Louis Page, who is being pursued by several top clubs in England, including Manchester United. The Red Devils already came close to signing the 18-year-old midfielder in the summer, but the move fell through. They continue to remain interested in the youngster but many other teams have now entered the fray. Real Madrid have watched Page According to the report, Real Madrid scouts have watched in action for Leicester City, with the club tracking more and more talents from England. The Merengues are already close to signing JJ Gabriel from Manchester United and seem to have identified Page as another prospect worth keeping an eye on. Louis Page is in demand. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) The 18-year-old starlet is a product of the Leicester City youth academy and made his first-team breakthrough for the Foxes last season. So far in the current campaign, the Englishman has made 15 senior appearances, scoring one and assisting five goals. Page has a contract with Leicester until the summer of 2029, but the English club are open to a sale in January provided two conditions are met. Firstly, they want the youngster to remain at the club on loan for the remainder of the season, and secondly they are seeking a total fee of £15 million (€18 million) for their prized asset. Plenty of competition for Page As mentioned earlier, there is no shortage of interest in Page, with Manchester United understood to be the club pushing the hardest for his signing. Manchester United are confident of signing Page. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Manchester City have also entered the race for the teenage midfielder, along with Chelsea and Arsenal. Other Premier League teams like Newcastle United, Aston Villa, and Brentford have also made enquiries. Outside of England, there has been interest from Borussia Dortmund, while Real Madrid’s arch-rivals, Barcelona have also watched him in action. For now, though, it is said that Manchester United remain confident of signing Page, who has six caps for the England U19 national team. Whether Real Madrid make a move for the teenager remains to be seen.

item.title: Seahawks QB Drew Lock dealing with ‘severe tendinitis’ ahead of Cardinals game
item.description: After fighting through an elbow injury, the Seattle Seahawks’ beloved backup signal caller will fill in for the Sam Darnold after the latter’s own injuries have forced him out. Drew Lock will make his second start this season, taking on the Arizona Cardinals once again. But the mystery of the elbow injury has now been solved, per Tom Pelissero. Seahawks QB Drew Lock has been battling severe tendinitis in his throwing elbow. But he looked good in limited practice reps and will start Sunday against Arizona in place of injured Sam Darnold, with free agency looming in March. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotsn76 pic.twitter.com/shgYQc9NTO — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 Lock’s availability was also somewhat in question this week, due to the tendinitis issue, but he apparently looked good enough in limited practice appearances to lead Seattle into a Week 9 divisional matchup. Lock made two appearances to start the season, posting a 127.3 passer rating (would lead the NFL if he had enough throws to qualify), 73% completion rate, 422 yards, 4 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. The hot start, coupled with turnover struggles from Sam Darnold, have had some fans clamoring to leave the backup inserted as the starter. A strained quad for Darnold will cause this idea to come to fruition for one week. The Arizona Cardinals defense has allowed the 2nd-most fantasy points to the QB position, so it will be interesting to see if big Lock lights it up again. Will the Seattle decision makers choose to ride the hot hand if the offense looks effective again, against a low-end opponent? Those are questions for another day. item.title: ‘I’d Have To Live With It’ — Todd McShay Identifies Scenario for NFL Teams To Draft Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith
item.description: ‘I’d Have To Live With It’ — Todd McShay Identifies Scenario for NFL Teams To Draft Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith The debate over the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft could come down to a familiar question for NFL teams: Should they prioritize positional value or take the best player available? Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is widely considered one of the top prospects in college football. However, NFL draft analyst Todd McShay believes there is a situation in which a team could pass on the talented receiver and select Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker instead. For teams desperately searching for a franchise quarterback, that decision might be easier than it sounds. Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith? McShay Explains Why During a discussion about the 2027 NFL Draft on “ The Triple Option” podcast , McShay was asked whether there was anyone in the class he would believe in enough to pass on Smith. The analyst pointed to Mestemaker, explaining, “We would have to have a plan organizationally, and I would have to have a strong belief in quarterback coach, but much more importantly, offensive coordinator slash head coach and in a developmental plan for Mestamaker, because we’re going to start him year one.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “I mean, that’s just how it works in the NFL. It’s just positional value. If we need one desperately, I’m not taking Jeremiah Smith over Mestamaker, and I’d have to live with it,” he added. McShay’s comments highlight the NFL’s emphasis on quarterbacks, as finding a franchise QB can change an organization’s future, even if Smith is the more talented prospect. Drew Mestemaker’s Rise Makes Him a Potential No. 1 Pick Mestemaker’s rise has been one of the more surprising stories in college football this season. The Oklahoma State quarterback was initially an unrated high school recruit and did not start a single varsity game at the position. He later walked on at North Texas before transferring to Oklahoma State for the 2026 season. Since arriving in Stillwater, Mestemaker has quickly climbed draft boards and established himself as one of the leading QB prospects in the 2027 class. A recent midseason poll of 25 NFL scouts and executives showed just how much his stock has increased. Seventeen of the 25 voters selected Mestemaker as their favorite to be the first quarterback taken in the draft. Mestemaker also holds an 83.9 grade, ranking 28th on PFN’s CFB QB Impact Rankings . Other prospects who could enter the conversation for the No. 1 overall pick include Texas’ Colin Simmons and Arch Manning, Miami’s Darian Mensah, and South Carolina’s Dylan Stewart. item.title: Furious Tottenham set to cite Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in formal complaint over Jayden Bogle's tackle at Leeds
item.description: Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham will lodge a formal complaint after Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel in the 1-0 defeat at Leeds. Tel was forced off before half-time, and Spurs believe the decision clashes with Jean-Philippe Mateta's dismissal against them a week earlier, while Roberto De Zerbi insisted he still has full confidence in the officials. Tottenham to write to Pro Ref over Bogle decision Tottenham will submit a formal complaint to refereeing body Pro Ref after Bogle avoided a red card during Saturday's 1-0 defeat to Leeds at Elland Road. According to the Independent, Spurs believe the defender should have been sent off, and they will write to Pro Ref to seek an explanation as to why the incident did not result in a dismissal. Bogle lunged into a first-half tackle on Tel and landed on the forward's ankle with his left foot. Referee John Brooks awarded a foul to Spurs, but he did not show Bogle a card or punish him any further. VAR stays out as Tel is forced off Play was paused while Tel received treatment on the pitch, and VAR Tony Harrington looked at the incident in detail. After a four-minute review, Harrington decided against sending Brooks to the pitchside monitor, and although the challenge was deemed "reckless", Bogle went unpunished. Tel came back on, but he was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes because of lingering effects on his Achilles. Leeds went on to win through a Noah Okafor goal, and speaking to the BBC, former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann said: "Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent. He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch." Mateta red card could strengthen Spurs' case Spurs may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Mateta for his foul on Micky van de Ven in their 2-0 win a week earlier. On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card, but it was upgraded after a VAR review. Later at Elland Road, Pedro Porro was booked for a challenge similar to Bogle's, which infuriated De Zerbi. De Zerbi was more critical of his own players after the game, but he said of the decision: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve. I was surprised on the yellow card for Pedro Porro because it was clear. The potential red card, I couldn't say. We have full confidence in the referee and VAR. I cannot say nothing more." Key Match Incidents Panel to review Bogle tackle The Key Match Incidents Panel will review the decision in the coming days, while Tottenham await an explanation from Pro Ref. Mateta, meanwhile, is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card.

item.title: Delaware at Kennesaw State in Conference USA football, live updates
item.description: KENNESAW, Georgia – Delaware ’s first football visit to Kennesaw State and Fifth Third Stadium holds reams of ramifications on Nov. 7. The Blue Hens (4-4 overall, 2-2 league) try to win Conference USA road games back-to-back for the first time in their two-year CUSA stay in the 3 p.m. kickoff (ESPN+). Kennesaw State, the defending CUSA champ, is expected to make that difficult. While the Owls may not appear particularly formidable with just two wins in eight games, momentum comes from last week’s 44-28 triumph at Middle Tennessee State, where Delaware recently lost. Kennesaw State is 1-3 in league games and cannot afford another defeat to remain bowl eligible. “They throw it and run it very explosively,” Delaware coach Ryan Carty said of the Owls, “And so we've got to make sure that we can get our stops on third downs and fourth downs. And then, probably most importantly, at some point we've got to cause some turnovers, some havoc.” When it has the ball, Delaware will be glad to have quarterback Nick Minicucci at the controls. Minicucci, who missed Delaware’s first two league games – both losses – with a knee injury, is coming off a record-setting win at Western Kentucky. item.title: Mikel Arteta identifies two missing elements that can raise Arsenal’s level
item.description: After a familiar scoreline, Mikel Arteta has a new phrase. The Arsenal manager used some variation on “insist” several times throughout his press conference for the win over Hull City, after his team had almost been left standing at the door. Martin Odegaard instead offered a captain’s goal, for a third 1-0 win in four in the league. Like many of those, it could have been worse, but could have been better – especially in terms of finishing. Arsenal currently always feel one setback away from a big discussion about which forward they need to sign in January. They are obviously monitoring a few options, and are expected to do some business, but Arteta clearly doesn’t want his players thinking like that. He put it down to something else. When asked about what was actually a sixth win by one goal out of 10 Premier League games so far, he said they “need to be more efficient”. It could be argued that such a return is the height of efficiency, and that Arsenal could have been further ahead had they benefited from that debated penalty decision – but you know what he meant, especially with regard to finishing. Arteta lamented how his team had two further one-on-ones in the game, only to waste them. He said it was like they “are trying to score the perfect goal”. That’s another familiar refrain with this club, if from a different era to the 1-0s. Arteta’s desired solution is to be “more pragmatic”, that they “need to be more chaotic”. That’s undeniably true, but the manager being the one to say this poses some questions of his own. Another phrase that Arteta used was “volume”. That, when you face a defence as well structured as Hull City, you need to be “generating volume”. In other words, numbers, a critical mass of chances where you eventually score – which is pretty much what they did. Insistence. Martin Odegaard took advantage inside the box to earn Arsenal a slender win (PA) It’s been discussed on these pages before that Arteta is a huge “probabilities guy”, where he sees almost every game as an equation. If Arsenal consistently generate an xG of 2 or above and limit the opposition to 0.5, they are likely to win enough games to win the league. A natural extension of this is an exactingly calibrated team, where Hull City players – like so many others – were left praising “the shape”. But is that mentality something that encourages “pragmatism” or, as Arteta elaborated, “chaos”? Other descriptions for that are sparkle, ingenuity… magic. That’s hard to find sufficient space for in a system that demands a lot of energy devoted to pressing and structure. Odegaard, the match-winner, is almost the ultimate example. The playmaker is capable of some of the most ingenious and exquisite touches in the league, but it does not feel like he is as characterised by that as much any more. item.title: The anatomy of an upset: Fort Valley State beats Florida A&M in early season action
item.description: The anatomy of an upset: Fort Valley State beats Florida A&M in early season action appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Early-season basketball is usually treated as an afterthought, specifically in HBCU basketball. Out-of-conference games across the board often look lopsided, and the more compelling matchups don’t come until after the turn of the new year. But a couple of early-season matchups are often worth your attention, such as Jackson State’s compelling victory over Tulane on Thursday evening. Another game worth a spotlight was Fort Valley State University’s 75-70 victory over the Charlie Ward-led Florida A&M Rattlers . The game was particularly exciting for me as a Fort Valley State University alumnus, but I think it shows an interesting trend for both Fort Valley State as they head into SIAC competition and things that Florida A&M needs to clean up. A slow start, then a run It did not look like an upset for most of the first half. The Wildcats shot 11-of-35 from the field and 3-of-16 from three, and they went into halftime down 34-28 at the Al Lawson Center. FAMU, in turn, shot 44 percent and had led by as many as seven. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Then Fort Valley came out of the break on a 19-5 run. In the first six minutes of the second half the Wildcats went from down six to up eight, 47-39. item.title: Nick Sirianni explains decision for Eagles QB change
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles added Joe Milton to the roster just a few weeks ago, but he’s already getting an opportunity to turn things around for a struggling Philadelphia offense. Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Friday and explained their decision to promote Milton and demote Tanner McKee in the process. “Obviously, that’s always a difficult thing to think through because it isn’t ever just on one person. Matter of fact, I think Tanner [McKee] played solid, but this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend.” Sirianni went on to say that Milton is talented and has been in Philly for a couple weeks, they’ve seen that he has a talented arm and is a talented athlete that can process and make decisions. “Just a lot of good qualities that [Joe Milton] has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it’s been fun getting to know him and working with him.” The head coach also explained that they felt it was best to make the move now instead of waiting for the bye week, because they are doing everything they can to win each and every game. “At the end of the day, I have to make the decision based off of that. But every decision that we make, we talk through in great, great detail. Obviously, Howie [Roseman] and I talk in great detail, the offensive staff and I, Parks [Frazier] and Sean [Mannion] and everybody. We just talk through it. At the end of the day, my job as the head coach is to make these decisions that I think is best for the football team, but you discuss everything with everybody.” Sirianni was asked about comments on Monday in support of Tanner McKee keeping his job. He revealed that they were fresh off the Sunday night game, and that was the initial plan, but after looking through the film and planning for the next game, they went in another direction. He also confirmed that while they made a change at quarterback, they did not make any changes to coaches roles. The head coach talked about how they look at everything when evaluating players, including that McKee was leading an offense decimated by injuries. Still, he noted that everyone still has to the best with whatever their circumstances may be, but they evaluate everyone fairly. Sirianni also threw his support to the entire QB room, saying he has always believed in the players they have at the position. He also defended his decision to withhold the information that they were making a change at quarterback, saying that he only tells the media what he wants, and that kind of decision is something he’ll want to hold onto for as long as possible. “Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. item.description: FILE PHOTO - Como manager Cesc Fàbregas gestures on the touchline during the pre season friendly soccer match between Arsenal and Como 1907 at Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Inter clash will be major test of Como's level, says Fàbregas») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Como boss Cesc Fàbregas says his side’s clash with Inter Milan will be a big test to see how much progress they have made. Second-placed Inter lost their unbeaten record in Serie A this season when they fell to a 3-1 defeat to derby rivals AC Milan last weekend and they will be looking to bounce back. Como are enjoying another impressive campaign themselves, sitting two places behind Inter, and are on a six-match winning run in all competitions, their latest victory a stunning 9-1 win away to Lens in the Champions League. Fàbregas told a press conference: “It feels like every week you ask me about a new test of our maturity. “We knew this season would be special for us, there is so much motivation, but we know our path. “This is an important match. We are coming off good form, but it is only a test to see where we can go. Inter remain the strongest team in Italy, we’ll see our level later.” Inter have proven Como’s bogey team since the latter were promoted in 2024. They have yet to beat Inter in the six meetings since their promotion, drawing only once in the first leg of a Coppa Italia semi-final and losing the rest. Fàbregas added: “We came close three times, but when Inter raise the bar, they become too strong for everyone. “We need to play our football, do our thing, without anxiety or pressure. After this match, we’ll see where we are. “I never stop learning from the best. The victory over Lens can happen once, if we’re lucky, in our lives, but Inter are the reigning champions of Italy, won the Coppa Italia, played two Champions League finals. “Who knows, tomorrow we might pull a surprise with the perfect performance.” Defeat to Milan saw Inter slip three points behind leaders Lazio. Inter captain Lautaro Martinez is unavailable for selection until after the international break through injury, while Luis Henrique is also out of the Como clash. However, Benjamin Pavard, John Stones and Curtis Jones have resumed training and could be in contention for Sunday’s game.

item.title: Press Room | Comments after Juventus Women-Sassuolo
item.description: Press Room | Comments after Juventus Women-Sassuolo The Women's First Team beat Sassuolo 2-1 in Biella on Matchday 6 of the Serie A Women season. Coach Isaac Guerrero and match-winner Cecilia Salvai spoke to the press after the match. ISAAC GUERRERO “This team has shown throughout the season that it possesses great qualities on the pitch, and when our play doesn’t quite reach its best – as was particularly the case in the first half – our heart, unity and team spirit come to the fore. It’s a team with a real spirit, and we can build a great deal on that. We’re enjoying a good run of positive results, but we want to keep improving in terms of our style of play as well. In the second half, we upped the tempo, moving the ball around more quickly and making better use of switches of play against a side that tended to sit deep. The girls did well to read the game and, above all, never gave up. Even after going 2–1 up, we kept pushing for a third goal, which shows the mentality of the squad. We now face a very busy period, with five matches in fifteen days. We’ll be facing one of the strongest teams in the world, but we have great confidence in our chances. With this spirit, we can compete against anyone. We’ll try to recover our energy as quickly as possible so that we’re ready.” CECILIA SALVAI “We conceded a goal that we could have avoided, and that made the match a bit more difficult, but we were aware of our strength. We had to be patient, keep believing in what we were doing, and in the end we managed to turn the game around. I’m happy about the goal, but above all about the win, because it was the result of great teamwork. Wednesday’s match against Lyon will be a completely different affair, we’re up against the most successful team in Europe in the Champions League, and we’ll have to pay close attention to every detail. However, we’re playing at home, we’re full of confidence and we’re in good form. We need to capitalise on this enthusiasm, whilst remaining aware that a very difficult challenge lies ahead.” Women | Juventus-Sassuolo | Gallery
